title: Aboriginal group demands meeting after RCMP shooting - Winnipeg Free Press
subtitle: Breaking News, Sports, Manitoba, Canada
article: This article was published 15/06/2008 (6286 days ago), so information in it may no longer be current.

CARLYLE, Sask. - The head of Saskatchewan's largest aboriginal organization is demanding a meeting with Canada's public safety minister, to talk about what he calls "Rambo-style" policing after RCMP shot and killed a man on a reserve southeast of Regina.
The man, identified by a relative as Chase McKay Standingready, 21, was fatally shot on the White Bear First Nation Saturday morning after police said he was armed with a knife.

Chief Lawrence Joseph of the Federation of Saskatchewan Indian Nations, says the latest shooting on the reserve near Carlyle, Sask., has raised questions about the policing of aboriginal people - something he says Stockwell Day should be concerned about, too.

In the wake of the federal apology Prime Minister Stephen Harper read last week to survivors of residential schools, Joseph says it's only natural that senior officials meet with aboriginal groups to discuss how to fix some of the problems those schools have spawned, like crime, rampant substance abuse and native gangs.
Joseph says they've made repeated requests to meet with Day, but those requests have been declined.

Brenda Standingready, 52, an aunt of the deceased man, says there's anger and shock in the community over the shooting of her nephew - a death she says might have been avoided had police used less lethal means to defuse the situation.
